comments.author: @AMT2025-s8z
comments.text:
*This isn’t an honest portrayal of India—it’s a carefully manufactured negative narrative.* 

You have made only seven videos, and all of them seem to focus on projecting and amplifying the negative side of those countries. This gives viewers a misleading and unfair image of the countries and their people. Some of the claims also appear to be based on your own assumptions or thinking rather than what is actually happening there.

You’ve deliberately searched for the worst-looking places, focused heavily on drainage, garbage, poverty, and a handful of disturbing scenes, and then presented them as though they represent all of India. That is not journalism or “showing the truth”—that is selective and misleading storytelling.

What’s even more concerning is that some of the scenes and stories you’ve shown appear to be limited to particular places—or, in some cases, questionable or poorly contextualized stories from only a few states—yet you present them as if they are the everyday reality of the entire country. A problem in one locality or one state does not automatically become a description of 1.4+ billion people across India.

If you genuinely wanted to show India honestly, you would show the good, the bad, and everything in between. Instead, you seem determined to collect the ugliest 5% and pretend it represents the remaining 95%.

India absolutely has serious problems, and they should be criticized. But criticism without context becomes propaganda. You cannot take isolated incidents, specific locations, or sensational stories and slap the label “This is India” on them.

If your intention was truly to show reality, then show the whole reality—not just the version that gets you views, outrage, and a convenient narrative.

India is not perfect, but your portrayal of India is far from complete either.
